newsitem.title: CHINA: China First Auto sets vehicle joint venture. [CORRECTED 06:28 GMT]
newsitem.headline: China First Auto sets vehicle joint venture. [CORRECTED 06:28 GMT]

text.p: China's First Automotive Corp has teamed with a major tobacco company and a regional vehicle producer in a joint venture aimed at conquering southern China's auto market, newspapers said on Friday.

First Automotive had a 51 percent stake in the new venture, while tobacco producer Yunnan Hongta Group held 30 percent (corrects from 39 percent) and Yunnan Light Vehicle (Group) Corp held the rest, the companies said in an announcement published in the Economic Daily.

The China Daily said officials of the State Planning Commission were surprised by the tobacco group's decision to invest in FAW Hongta Yunnan Automotive Manufacturing Co, but had no plans to interfere.

The latest venture by First Automotive, which is based in northeastern China's Jilin province, was a major move into a southern market long dominated by rival Dongfeng Motor Group, the newspaper said.

It gave no details of the scale of investment in the venture or of its production plans. First Automotive already produces heavy and light trucks and buses and has a joint venture with Germany's Volkswagen AG that makes Jetta sedans.
Beijing has called for a major consolidation of Chinese automakers, many of which still run small and often inefficient production lines.

FAW Hongta Yunnan was part of a drastic restructuring process that would turn 120 local producers into three or four internationally competitive groups by 2000, the China Daily quoted Vice Minister of Machinery Industry Lu Fuyuan as saying.
